- `printer_manual_setup` opens Orca’s printer list and reports what the person added there. It may be a useful handoff, but the guide asks for evidence that a separate tool is needed.
- `printer_manual_connection` only opens a settings window.
- `printer_setup_finish` only closes the panel.

Those last two look like the UI controls the [guide says not to add tools for](/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md:44). The guide also says to use [call logs and evals to decide consolidation](/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md:85); the [printer prompt tests](/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/tests/printer_prompt/README.md) exercise journeys, but do not compare this eight-tool design with fewer tools or direct UI controls.

There is a documentation mismatch to resolve: the [guide still says one tool loads per mode](/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md:95), while the code and tests say eight load in each. **Yes, the agent should be able to decide that a manual handoff would help. I would not make “open this system dialog” the default shape of an agent tool.** The agent can offer a specific action, such as “Browse the full printer list,” and the app can open the dialog when the person taps it. That keeps dialog mechanics in the UI while letting the agent guide the conversation.

That distinction matters for the three current tools:

| Tool | Assessment |
|---|---|
| `printer_manual_setup` | Borderline. It returns which printers the person added, so it does more than open a window. But the app already has a direct menu action that opens the wizard and reports the result to the conversation. A separate model tool has no demonstrated need. |
| `printer_manual_connection` | Weak case. It opens settings and returns only `opened`; the person does the work. The app already has a direct menu action. |
| `printer_setup_finish` | UI navigation. Back already closes the panel directly; tapping Done could do the same without another model call. |

Those direct paths are in [App.tsx](/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/App.tsx:397) and [PrinterConversation.cpp](/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp:626). The guide’s general rule also rejects tools that merely automate a UI control ([tool guide](/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md:44)).

**If every native dialog gets a corresponding tool, the catalog will grow quickly.** Each definition is offered to the model on turns where it is exposed, even when never called; calls add another round trip. Caching can reduce repeated token cost, but it does not remove tool selection complexity. The sustainable unit is a *printer operation with distinct inputs, results, or authorization*—such as connecting with a credential—not a dialog. A generic `open_dialog` tool would merely hide the same growing list in an action parameter.

Per-mode exposure also needs tightening. [The current profile](/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp:138) offers all eight in all three modes, and the tool handlers do not enforce mode boundaries. I would expose the operations valid for each conversation’s workflow, account for Add naturally continuing into Connect, and enforce the target and allowed action in native code. If the person changes tasks mid-conversation, the app can make that transition explicitly. That is a better reason to change the available tools than giving every session every capability.
So the three use cases range from borderline to weakness. and your conclusion became "the agent should be able to decide that a manual handoff would help.". am i missing anything?

No. My conclusion was too soft.

For these three cases, I don’t see a justified need for an agent tool. The agent can **suggest** a manual step, but the app can present a button for the person to open the dialog. `printer_setup_finish` is simply navigation. `printer_manual_connection` only opens a window. `printer_manual_setup` returns useful results, but the existing direct UI path already sends those results back to the conversation.

So my recommendation is to remove those three from the model’s tool list, keep the direct UI actions, and evaluate the remaining printer tools by workflow. “The agent can recognize when a handoff would help” does **not** imply “the agent needs a tool to open the dialog.”
